pairs: Fuit quidam vir Levites habitans in latere montis Ephraim,
There was a certain man, a Levite, living beside mount Ephraim,
qui accepit uxorem de Bethlehem Juda:
who took a wife from Bethlehem of Judah.
et reversa est in domum patris sui in Bethlehem,
and she returned to the house of her father in Bethlehem.
And she stayed with him for four months.
wishing to be reconciled with her,
and to speak kindly to her,
and to lead her back with him.
habens in comitatu puerum et duos asinos:
And he had with him a servant and two donkeys.
et introduxit in domum patris sui.
and brought him into the house of her father.
And when his father-in-law had heard about this,
Mansitque gener in domo soceri tribus diebus,
And the son-in-law stayed in the house of his father-in-law for three days,
comedens cum eo et bibens familiariter.
eating and drinking with him in a friendly manner.
Die autem quarto de nocte consurgens,
But on the fourth day, arising in the night,
quem tenuit socer, et ait ad eum:
But his father-in-law took hold of him,
and he said to him, “First taste a little bread,
and then you shall set out.”
Dixitque pater puellæ ad generum suum:
And the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law,
Quæso te ut hodie hic maneas,
“I ask you to remain here today,
so that we may rejoice together.”
At ille consurgens, cœpit velle proficisci.
But getting up, he intended to begin to set out.
Et nihilominus obnixe eum socer tenuit,
But nevertheless, his father-in-law pressed him resolutely,
and made him remain with him.
the Levite was preparing for his journey.
Cui socer rursum: Oro te, inquit,
And his father-in-law said to him again,
“I beg you to take a little food,
et assumptis viribus donec increscat dies,
and to be strengthened, until the daylight increases,
and after that, you shall set out.”
And the young man got up,
so that he might travel with his wife and servant.
And his father-in-law spoke to him again:
Considera quod dies ad occasum declivior sit,
and spend the day in gladness.
And tomorrow you shall set out,
et cras proficisceris ut vadas in domum tuam.
so that you may go to your own house.”
His son-in-law was not willing to agree to his words. Instead,
which by another name is called Jerusalem,
leading with him two donkeys carrying burdens,
And now they were near Jebus,
but day was turning into night.
And the servant said to his lord,
let us turn aside to the city of the Jebusites,
so that we may find lodging in it.”
“I will not enter into the town of a foreign people,
quæ non est de filiis Israël:
who are not of the sons of Israel. Instead,
I will cross over as far as Gibeah.
And when I will have arrived there,
we will lodge in that place,
or at least in the city of Ramah.”
and continuing on, they undertook the journey.
But the sun went down on them when they were near Gibeah,
which is of the tribe of Benjamin.
And so they diverted to it,
so that they might lodge there.
they were sitting in the street of the city.
et nullus eos recipere voluit hospitio.
For no one was willing to give them hospitality.

qui et ipse de monte erat Ephraim,
and he was also from mount Ephraim,
and he was living as a stranger in Gibeah.
homines autem regionis illius erant filii Jemini.
For the men of that region were of the sons of Benjamin.
And the old man, lifting up his eyes,
vidit senex sedentem hominem cum sarcinulis suis in platea civitatis,
saw the man sitting with his bundles in the street of the city. And he said to him:
“We set out from Bethlehem of Judah,
and we are traveling to our own place,
qui est in latere montis Ephraim,
From there we went to Bethlehem,
et nunc vadimus ad domum Dei,
and now we go to the house of God.
nullusque sub tectum suum nos vult recipere,
But no one is willing to receive us under his roof.
habentes paleas et fœnum in asinorum pabulum,
We have straw and hay as fodder for the donkeys,
et panem ac vinum in meos et ancillæ tuæ usus,
and we have bread and wine for the use of myself,
and for your handmaid and the servant who is with me.
And the old man responded to him:
ego præbebo omnia quæ necessaria sunt:
I will provide all that is necessary.
do not stay in the street.”
And he led him into his house,
and he gave fodder to his donkeys.
And after they had washed their feet,
he received them with a banquet.
et post laborem itineris cibo et potu reficientibus corpora,
and were refreshing their bodies with food and drink after the labor of the journey,
came and surrounded the old man’s house.
And they began to knock at the door,
clamantes ad dominum domus atque dicentes:
calling out to the lord of the house,
“Bring out the man who entered your house,
so that we may abuse him.”
And the old man went out to them,
do not choose to do this evil.
quia ingressus est homo hospitium meum:
For this man has entered to my hospitality.
And you must cease from this senselessness.
and this man has a mate.

ne scelus hoc contra naturam operemini in virum.
do not commit this crime against nature on the man.”

eduxit ad eos concubinam suam, et eis tradidit illudendam:
led out his mate to them, and he delivered her to their sexual abuse.
qua cum tota nocte abusi essent,
And when they had abused her for the entire night,
they released her in the morning.
came to the door of the house,

et ecce concubina ejus jacebat ante ostium sparsis in limine manibus.
And behold, his mate was lying before the door, with her hands reaching out to the threshold.
But since she gave no response,
and he laid her on his donkey,
and he returned to his house.
et cadaver uxoris cum ossibus suis in duodecim partes ac frustra concidens,
and he cut into pieces the dead body of his wife, with her bones, into twelve parts.
And he sent the pieces into all the parts of Israel.
And when each one had seen this,
Numquam res talis facta est in Israël,
“Never has such a thing been done in Israel,
ex eo die quo ascenderunt patres nostri de Ægypto usque in præsens tempus:
from the day that our fathers ascended from Egypt,
et in commune decernite quid facto opus sit.
Let a sentence be brought and let us decide in common what ought to be done.”
